questions.q: Why can input drift and score drift serve as the early warning for this model, while precision at the top 10% cannot?
options: Precision is not a real metric
Precision needs the true outcome, which is only known 60 days after each list is produced
Drift metrics are more accurate than precision
The model has no scores until labels arrive
questions.explain: The label is 'cancels within 60 days', so ground-truth performance lags by two months. Drift metrics need only the incoming features and scores, so they are available immediately.

questions.q: What does a PSI of 0.607 on order_rate (against an alert threshold of 0.25) tell you?
options: The order_rate distribution in the new data differs strongly from the training sample, and someone should investigate
The model's accuracy dropped by 60.7%
The order_rate column contains 60.7% missing values
The model must be retrained automatically
questions.explain: PSI measures how far a distribution has moved from the reference. It flags a change in inputs, which needs investigation; it does not by itself prove degraded performance or dictate an automatic retrain.

questions.q: Why was a control comparison (the untouched test set against the training sample) run before the simulated shift?
options: To increase the test set size
Because a shift cannot be simulated without a control
To retrain the model
To show that PSI thresholds do not fire on ordinary sampling noise: the control never exceeded 0.025
questions.explain: A monitor that alarms on normal variation gets ignored. Showing that unchanged data stays far below 0.10 builds confidence that alerts mean something.

questions.q: The plan sets a watch at precision 0.32 and an alert at 0.25 for a 369-customer cycle. What guided these numbers?
options: They are standard values that never change
They equal the average precision of the model
The measured noise (standard error of about 0.026), the 0.32 ambition target, and the 0.208 break-even
They were copied from the test set's confidence interval
questions.explain: Thresholds should reflect how noisy the check is and what the business needs. 0.32 is about three standard errors below current performance; 0.25 is within about two of break-even.

questions.q: Which statement about drift is correct?
options: Drift in any feature always means the model is degrading
Drift is not degradation: an unimportant feature can drift harmlessly, and concept drift can hurt performance with no input drift
If inputs do not drift, the model cannot degrade
Drift only matters for deep learning models
questions.explain: Input monitoring is a proxy. That is why the plan includes performance monitoring on delayed labels, and why alerts lead to investigation before action.
